questions.prompt: The poet was writing verses about the ancient war.
questions.answer: Poēta versūs dē bellō antīquō scrībēbat.

questions.prompt: The boy read the letter which his father had sent.
questions.answer: Puer epistulam lēgit quam pater mīserat.

questions.prompt: The teacher will lead the pupils into the temple.
questions.answer: Magister discipulōs in templum dūcet.

questions.prompt: We rule the province justly and defend its borders.
questions.answer: Prōvinciam iūstē regimus et fīnēs dēfendimus.

questions.prompt: The commander sent scouts so that they might learn the enemy's plans.
questions.answer: Imperātor explōrātōrēs mīsit ut hostium cōnsilia cognōscerent.

questions.prompt: If you ruled the city wisely, the people would love you.
questions.answer: Sī urbem sapienter regerēs, populus tē amāret.

questions.prompt: May the gods rule the affairs of mortals with kindness.
questions.answer: Deī rēs mortālium cum benignitāte regant.

questions.prompt: The tyrant had ruled the island for many years.
questions.answer: Tyrannus īnsulam multōs annōs rēxerat.

questions.prompt: When you have written the book, send it to me.
questions.answer: Cum librum scrīpseris, eum ad mē mitte.

questions.prompt: By dawn the army will have driven the enemy from the walls.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce exercitus hostēs ā mūrīs ēgerit.

questions.prompt: Ruling with justice, the king held the love of the people.
questions.answer: Cum iūstitiā regēns, rēx amōrem populī tenēbat.

questions.prompt: Those about to rule must first learn to obey.
questions.answer: Rēctūrī prīmum pārēre discere dēbent.

questions.prompt: The general, leading his troops, advanced into enemy territory.
questions.answer: Dux cōpiās dūcēns in fīnēs hostium prōgressus est.

questions.prompt: Writing many books, the old man taught the young.
questions.answer: Multōs librōs scrībēns, senex iuvenēs docēbat.

questions.prompt: Rule your own spirit, and you will rule others well.
questions.answer: Animum tuum rege, et aliōs bene regēs.

questions.prompt: The waves were driving the shattered ship toward the rocks.
questions.answer: Undae nāvem frāctam ad saxa agēbant.

questions.prompt: The farmers cultivate the fields which their ancestors left them.
questions.answer: Agricolae agrōs colunt quōs maiōrēs eīs relīquērunt.

questions.prompt: Seek peace, citizens, but do not fear war.
questions.answer: Pācem petite, cīvēs, sed bellum nōlīte timēre.

questions.prompt: While the crops were growing thickly, the farmer ruled his household with care.
questions.answer: Dum segetēs dēnsē crēscēbant, agricola familiam suam cūrā regēbat.

questions.prompt: Before dawn the general led his troops across the swollen river.
questions.answer: Ante lūcem dux cōpiās suās trāns flūmen tumidum dūxit.

questions.prompt: Whoever rules the seas will rule the whole world.
questions.answer: Quisquis maria reget, tōtum orbem reget.

questions.prompt: Having conquered the enemy, the consul established new laws.
questions.answer: Hostibus victīs, cōnsul novās lēgēs cōnstituit.

questions.prompt: The wise king used to rule the people with gentle authority.
questions.answer: Rēx sapiēns populum mītī auctōritāte regēbat.

questions.prompt: Let the gods rule our minds, and let us follow their laws.
questions.answer: Regant deī mentēs nostrās, et lēgēs eōrum sequāmur.

questions.prompt: The soldiers were driving the frightened horses toward the dense forest.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs equōs territōs ad silvam dēnsam agēbant.

questions.prompt: If you had ruled justly, the citizens would have loved you.
questions.answer: Sī iūstē rēxissēs, cīvēs tē amāvissent.

questions.prompt: The just king ruled the wide kingdom with a gentle hand for many years.
questions.answer: Rēx iūstus lātum rēgnum manū lēnī multōs per annōs rēxit.

questions.prompt: While the soldiers were fighting bravely, the general led fresh troops into the battle.
questions.answer: Dum mīlitēs fortiter pugnant, dux integrās cōpiās in proelium dūxit.

questions.prompt: May the gods lead us safely across the stormy sea to our homeland.
questions.answer: Dī nōs per pelagus turbidum tūtōs in patriam dūcant.

questions.prompt: If you had written the letter sooner, I would have sent help at once.
questions.answer: Sī epistulam citius scrīpsissēs, auxilium statim mīsissem.

questions.prompt: The old man, ruling his household wisely, taught his grandsons the ancient laws.
questions.answer: Senex, domum suam sapienter regēns, nepōtēs lēgēs antīquās docuit.

questions.prompt: Whoever conquers his own desires rules a greater kingdom than kings.
questions.answer: Quīcumque cupiditātēs suās vincit, māius rēgnum quam rēgēs regit.

questions.prompt: Let us seek peace, citizens, and let us defend the laws of our ancestors.
questions.answer: Petāmus pācem, cīvēs, et lēgēs māiōrum nostrōrum dēfendāmus.

questions.prompt: By nightfall the enemy will have driven our cavalry from the plain.
questions.answer: Sub noctem hostēs equitēs nostrōs ex campō ēgerint.

questions.prompt: The general, about to lead his army across the river, strengthened the soldiers with words.
questions.answer: Dux, exercitum trāns flūmen ductūrus, mīlitēs verbīs firmāvit.

questions.prompt: The consul was ruling the province when the messenger announced the war.
questions.answer: Cōnsul prōvinciam regēbat, cum nūntius bellum nūntiāvit.

questions.prompt: Rule the people justly, and they will never fear your power.
questions.answer: Rege populum iūstē, et potestātem tuam numquam timēbunt.

questions.prompt: When the tribune had led his men back into the camp, he wrote a long letter.
questions.answer: Tribūnus, cum mīlitēs in castra redūxisset, longam epistulam scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: The city is ruled by a just king.
questions.answer: Urbs ā rēge iūstō regitur.

questions.prompt: The captives were being led through the streets by the soldiers.
questions.answer: Captīvī per viās ā mīlitibus dūcēbantur.

questions.prompt: Letters are sent to the general every day.
questions.answer: Litterae ad ducem cotīdiē mittuntur.

questions.prompt: The song was being sung by the old woman in the garden.
questions.answer: Carmen ab anū in hortō canēbātur.

questions.prompt: You will be ruled by wiser laws.

questions.prompt: The bonds will be loosened by the fleeing prisoner.
questions.answer: Vincula ā captīvō fugiente dissolventur.

questions.prompt: The enemy will be conquered before winter.
questions.answer: Hostēs ante hiemem vincentur.

questions.prompt: These words will be written on lasting stone.
questions.answer: Haec verba in saxō mānsūrō scrībentur.

questions.prompt: The town had been abandoned by its citizens before the war.
questions.answer: Oppidum ā cīvibus ante bellum relictum erat.

questions.prompt: The general has been conquered by his own arrogance.
questions.answer: Dux superbiā suā victus est.

questions.prompt: Many temples were erected by the ancient kings.
questions.answer: Multa templa ā rēgibus antīquīs exstrūcta sunt.

questions.prompt: The secret plan had been uncovered by a treacherous slave.

questions.prompt: He fights bravely so that his homeland may not be oppressed.
questions.answer: Fortiter pugnat nē patria opprimātur.

questions.prompt: They fled lest they be conquered by the enemy.
questions.answer: Fūgērunt nē ab hostibus vincerentur.

questions.prompt: The messenger hurried so that the letter might be delivered quickly.
questions.answer: Nūntius festīnāvit ut epistula celeriter redderētur.

questions.prompt: With the city captured, the survivors were led into slavery.
questions.answer: Urbe captā superstitēs in servitūtem ductī sunt.

questions.answer: Quercus antīqua saeviente tempestāte frācta est.

questions.prompt: Once the signal had been given, the ships were led out of the harbor.
questions.answer: Signō datō nāvēs ē portū ēductae sunt.

questions.answer: Lūcus sacer ab agricolīs timidīs colitur.

questions.prompt: If the walls had been defended, the town would not have been taken.

questions.prompt: Be led by reason, not by anger.
questions.answer: Ratiōne, nōn īrā, dūcere.

questions.prompt: The weary soldiers would be pressed down by the long march.
questions.answer: Fessī mīlitēs longō itinere dēprimerentur.

questions.prompt: The gates of the city are closed by the vigilant guards at night.
questions.answer: Portae urbis noctū ā vigilibus custōdibus clauduntur.

questions.answer: Agrī ab agricolīs colēbantur antequam imbrēs venīrent.

questions.answer: Grave onus tergō fessī mūlī impositum est.

questions.prompt: You will be led into the temple by the priests tomorrow.
questions.answer: Crās ā sacerdōtibus in templum dūcēris.

questions.prompt: Let the walls be defended lest the city be overthrown.
questions.answer: Mūrī dēfendantur nē urbs ēvertātur.

questions.prompt: The bridge had been broken by the river before the army arrived.

questions.prompt: These gifts are placed upon the altar by devout women.
questions.answer: Haec dōna ā piīs mulieribus in ārā pōnuntur.

questions.prompt: May you be defended by the gods in every danger.
questions.answer: In omnī perīculō ā deīs dēfendāris.

questions.prompt: The war will be waged fiercely by the united tribes.

questions.prompt: If the truth had been sought, the crime would have been uncovered.
questions.answer: Sī vērum quaesītum esset, scelus patefactum esset.

questions.prompt: We are pressed on all sides by a cruel enemy.
questions.answer: Undique ā crūdēlī hoste premimur.

questions.prompt: The secret letters will be entrusted to a faithful messenger before dawn.
questions.answer: Litterae arcānae ante lūcem fīdēlī nūntiō committentur.

questions.prompt: The general was being surrounded by the enemy while he fought bravely.
questions.answer: Dux ab hostibus cingēbātur dum fortiter pugnat.

questions.prompt: Let these things be understood by all before we depart.
questions.answer: Haec ab omnibus intellegantur antequam discēdimus.

questions.answer: Rētia ā piscātōribus ex altō marī trahuntur.

questions.prompt: The seeds were scattered across the field by the diligent hand of the farmer.
questions.answer: Sēmina dīligentī agricolae manū per agrum sparsa sunt.

questions.prompt: The camp had been left behind by the fleeing soldiers before nightfall.
questions.answer: Castra ā fugientibus mīlitibus ante noctem relicta erant.

questions.answer: Tantō pondere obruerēris nisi deī tē adiuvārent.

questions.prompt: Recall the journeys which our generals have made through these years, in Italy, through the fields and towns of Roman citizens.
questions.answer: Itinera quae per hōsce annōs in Ī̆taliā per agrōs atque oppida cīvium Rōmānōrum nostrī imperātōrēs fēcerint, recordāminī.

questions.prompt: Nothing was left to Caesar except to harass and wear down the enemy's column with his cavalry.
questions.answer: Relinquēbātur Caesarī nihil, nisi utī equitātū agmen adversāriōrum male habēret et carperet.

questions.prompt: But I, for a definite reason, am not yet brought to do this thing, which ought to have been done long ago.
questions.answer: Vērum ego hoc, quod iam prīdem factum esse oportuit, certa dē causā nōndum addūcor ut faciam.

questions.prompt: Similar is the method of the oat, which, sown in autumn, is partly cut for hay or fodder while it is still green, and partly kept for seed.
questions.answer: Similis ratiō avēnae est, quae autumnō sata partim caeditur in faenum vel pābulum dum adhūc viret, partim sēminī custōdītur.

questions.answer: Ō dī immortālēs! nōn intellegunt hominēs, quam magnum vectīgal sit parsimōnia.

questions.prompt: I will not bring up what is inconsistent with my character, and yet I will act in such a way that you understand what these men feel about you.
questions.answer: Nōn referam id quod abhorret ā meīs mōribus, et tamen faciam ut intellegās quid hī dē tē sentiant.

questions.prompt: He, on the contrary, signals with his hand that the other should wait a little, and again bends over his wax tablets and stylus.
questions.answer: Hic contrā ut paulum exspectāret manū significat rursusque cērīs et stilō incumbit.

questions.prompt: Perhaps you will ask what I myself am doing, I who give you these precepts.
questions.answer: Interrogābis fortasse quid ego faciam quī tibi ista praecipiō.

questions.answer: Exspectās fortasse dum dīcat.

questions.prompt: I am waiting in the villa at Arcae until I find this out.
questions.answer: Ego in Arcānō opperior dum ista cōgnōscō.

questions.prompt: So long as the Gauls were at a distance from the fortifications, they had the advantage because of their missiles.
questions.answer: Dum longius ā mūnītiōne aberant Gallī, plūs multitūdine tēlōrum prōficiēbant.

questions.prompt: While this was going on, a message was brought to Caesar.
questions.answer: Dum haec geruntur, Caesarī nūntiātum est.

questions.prompt: I cannot help sending to you every day.

questions.prompt: It was out of the question that Cleomenes should not be spared.
questions.answer: Fierī nūllō modō poterat quīn Cleomenī parcerētur.
